text:
carla: Quick design question — I'm sketching a per-org rate policy that uses RPM (requests/min), TPM (tokens/min) and a concurrency cap. Want feedback before I formalize. Thinking: primary enforcement per-org across all API keys, with per-key overrides for partners.

ben: Do we count tokens as input+output or just generated tokens?

carla: input+output. We want customers to be billed/limited on total token work. We can expose both if folks want separate telemetry.

alice: 👍 For enforcement, are we planning strict 429s or soft queuing? queuing adds complexity to runtime.

carla: leaning toward hybrid: short adaptive queue (100–500ms) for small bursts, otherwise immediate 429 with Retry-After. Makes UX nicer without a big runtime change. Thoughts?

dan: If we do adaptive queue we need to bound memory and avoid head-of-line blocking across orgs. Also, concurrency cap should be enforced first — it's simplest to implement at the gateway.

elena: Telemetry note: emit these metrics per org and per route: `org.rpm`, `org.tpm`, `org.concurrent`, `org.burst_credits`. Console should show 1h/24h heatmaps and a threshold alert at 80% of quota.

ben: Config example might help. Proposed minimal policy snippet:

```yaml
policy:
  org_quota:
    rpm: 1200           # requests per minute
    tpm: 600000         # tokens per minute (input+output)
    concurrency: 40     # simultaneous inflight requests
    burst_credits: 6    # number of short extra concurrent slots
    burst_window: 10s   # window used to replenish credits
```

alice: +1 to credits model. Implementation detail: use token-bucket for RPM/TPM and a separate semaphore for concurrency. Burst credits can be consumed from a small leaky bucket.

carla: Agreed. Also want per-org aggregation across API keys: all keys for org X share the same buckets. But allow partner keys to have `override_policy` flag for higher caps. This keeps pricing simple.

dan: Two concerns: 1) enforcement location — gateway vs control plane? 2) race conditions when keys route to different edge nodes.

carla: For (1) enforcement at the edge with local caches of the org state plus periodic sync to control plane; control plane is the source of truth. For (2) use consistent hashing of org id to a short-lived lease/token at the gateway layer or use a lightweight distributed counter (redis per region) for concurrency. We should quantify added latency.

elena: For telemetry -> make sure we tag metrics with `model`, `route`, `deployment_region`. We also need a derived metric `org.capacity_utilization = max(rpm/rpm_quota, tpm/tpm_quota, concurrent/concurrency_quota)` to drive console warnings.

ben: How do we handle billing vs enforcement? If customers hit TPM but not RPM, do we throttle or bill then throttle?

carla: Enforcement first, billing later. But console should surface predicted overages and a permissive mode where customers get warnings for N days before hard throttle (opt-in). This is useful for migrations.

alice: UX: in Console -> per-org overview card with live tokens/min and concurrent in-flight, plus dropdown to view active keys and per-key overrides. Add an action: "request temporary burst" that creates a ticket/auto-approval flow.

dan: One more ops edge-case: burst credits reset policy. If window is too short, noisy neighbors can starve others. Suggest credits be replenished slowly (exponential backoff) and add a global emergency reserve for platform stability.

carla: Good call. I'll add an explicit `reserve_pool` in the doc and a kill-switch that SRE can toggle.

infra-bot: deploy-canary: per-org-rate-limiter v0.1 -> canary started in eu-west-1 (10% traffic). Logs: 15% of requests received 429 within first 20m.

carla: Thanks infra-bot. Ben/Elena/Alice/Dan — can you review the design doc I'm about to open (link: https://redwood.internal/designs/per-org-rate-policy) and leave comments by EOD? I'll file the implementation ticket after that.

ben: will review.

alice: on it.

dan: quick pass now.

elena: leaving telemetry notes in the doc. :+1:
